description: AZ-Hydro is a 2 km gridded dataset of annual groundwater and surface-water withdrawals, irrigation consumptive use and pumping-induced stream capture for Arizona from 1896 to 2099, with combined uncertainty bands, basin and subbasin time series, and a per-well package. Researchers at the Desert Research Institute and Colorado State University with the Arizona Department of Water Resources produced it and publish the outputs, input data, models, validation and software on Zenodo and GitHub as a free download under CC BY 4.0 (version 1.1.0, July 2026, which renamed the stream capture product). Coverage is the state of Arizona, historical and projected. Caveats: the full archive is very large (about 88 GB compressed), the companion papers were still in preparation, and projections depend on the scenarios used. Simulation uses: groundwater and surface-water demand for regional water supply capacity planning, drought and climate adaptation studies and basin network models. Related records: USGS monthly irrigation water use by HUC12 (data-usgs-monthly-irrigation-water-use-huc12-2015) and USGS public-supply water use (data-usgs-public-supply-water-use-reanalysis-huc12).
name: AZ-Hydro, historical and projected Arizona annual water use at 2 km (1896-2099)
provider: Desert Research Institute, Colorado State University and Arizona Department of Water Resources (S. Majumdar, R. G. Smith, P. ReVelle, M. F. Hasan, W. Collin)
